text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Saturday said the dollar's correction should be completed now, but that the G7 summit was unlikely to come up with a formal agreement on the U.S. currency.

Speaking at a breakfast briefing before meetings with the six other most industrialised member nations which are part of the G-7, Tietmeyer said: "the dollar correction process ought to end about now."
At the same time Tietmeyer added, "The mark remains a stable and therefore strong currency."

The dollar has appreciated sharply in recent weeks against the mark, recovering from the historic lows it reached in the spring on 1995. Waigel added that the dollar's moves signal an orderly recovery, saying: "The orderly reversal sought by the G7 has taken place."
Asked whether he could visualise the G7 setting a formal agreement to stop the dollar from rising, Waigel said:" "I cannot imagine a formal agreement."
Waigel also stressed that the dollar gains were not due to the failings of Germany or Europe. The U.S. Germany, Japan, France, Italy, Canada and Britain are members of the G7.
